intents.name: Cache Locality & Data Reuse
intents.description: Optimize memory access patterns and exploit temporal/spatial locality through hierarchical tiling aligned with L1/L2/L3 cache sizes.
intents.rationale: Convolution kernels are memory-bandwidth-limited on CPUs. Strategic tiling reduces cache misses and enables data reuse across the K×H×W computation. With L1d~32KB, L2~256KB per core, and output dimensions OH×OW, blocking the spatial output and filter dimensions to fit in cache hierarchy is critical for sustained throughput.

transformations.name: Tile Output Spatial Dimensions
transformations.description: Block the output spatial dimensions (OH, OW) into cache-friendly tile sizes (e.g., 8×8 or 16×16) to maximize reuse of input activations and filter weights within L2.
transformations.rationale: Each output tile reuses the same filter weights and input patches across multiple output points. Tiling enables these values to stay resident in cache, reducing main-memory traffic.

transformations.name: Tile Filter Dimension
transformations.description: Partition the filter/feature dimension F into blocks that fit within L3 or shared L2 capacity, processing multiple output channels per cache block.
transformations.rationale: Reduces L3 misses when iterating over output channels; enables amortization of input reloads across multiple output channels per tile.

transformations.name: Tile Input Channel Dimension
transformations.description: Block the input channel dimension C into strips that fit in L2, reusing the same spatial tiles of input across multiple channel blocks.
transformations.rationale: Keeps input spatial patches (H×W per channel block) in L2 while iterating over input channels, reducing capacity misses and improving spatial locality.

transformations.name: Tile Batch Dimension
transformations.description: Partition batch dimension N into smaller groups to improve cache efficiency by processing fewer independent output maps simultaneously.
transformations.rationale: Reduces peak memory footprint per tile and improves cache utilization when N is large; enables better data locality for batched operations.

intents.name: SIMD Vectorization
intents.description: Expose and exploit AVX2 vector parallelism (256-bit, 8×FP32 or 4×FP64 lanes) through loop restructuring and memory layout optimization.
intents.rationale: AVX2 provides 8 lanes for FP32 and 4 lanes for FP64. Convolution innermost loops over C (input channels) or F (output features) can be vectorized if data is properly aligned and contiguous. Vectorization improves throughput by 4–8×.

transformations.name: Vectorize Channel/Feature Accumulation Loop
transformations.description: Restructure the accumulation loop over input channels (C) or output features (F) to enable SIMD reduction with vectorized FP operations and proper alignment.
transformations.rationale: The innermost reduction over C or F can be vectorized with explicit vector instructions; reduces scalar loop overhead and enables pipelined FP units.

transformations.name: Memory Layout Optimization for Vectorization
transformations.description: Transpose or reshape tensors so that the vectorizable dimension (C or F) is contiguous and aligned to 32 or 64 bytes.
transformations.rationale: Aligned, contiguous access patterns are required for efficient vector loads/stores; misaligned or strided access degrades to scalar operations or requires penalties.

transformations.name: Unroll Vectorized Loops
transformations.description: Unroll the vectorized innermost loop by a small factor (2–4) to expose multiple independent vector operations for out-of-order execution.
transformations.rationale: Reduces control-flow overhead and allows the CPU to execute multiple FMA (fused multiply-add) instructions in parallel, improving ILP and FU utilization.

intents.name: Loop Fusion & Kernel Decomposition
intents.description: Merge or decompose convolution operations into lower-level loop nests to enable joint optimization and reduce intermediate memory traffic.
intents.rationale: The generic linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw is a high-level operation. Decomposing it into explicit nested loops (or fusing with surrounding operations) exposes transformation opportunities and eliminates unnecessary intermediate materializations.

transformations.name: Decompose Convolution to Nested Loops
transformations.description: Expand linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw into explicit nested loops over N, F, OH, OW, C, KH, KW to enable fine-grained loop transformations.
transformations.rationale: Exposes the full loop structure for subsequent tiling, vectorization, and interchange; generic operations often prevent application of loop-level optimizations.

transformations.name: Im2Col Transformation (Implicit)
transformations.description: Restructure the convolution loop nest to group spatial patches into column-wise blocks, conceptually converting convolution into matrix multiplication.
transformations.rationale: Im2Col-like restructuring can expose matrix-multiplication-like structure that benefits from GEMM-style tiling and vectorization; enables reuse of BLAS-like optimization techniques.

intents.name: Loop Ordering & Interchange
intents.description: Reorder loops to improve cache locality, data reuse, and vectorization by placing memory-access-intensive dimensions in optimal positions.
intents.rationale: Loop order affects the sequence of memory accesses. Moving compute-heavy or reuse-rich dimensions (e.g., C, F) closer to innermost positions improves cache behavior and vectorization.

transformations.name: Interchange Output Spatial & Channel Loops
transformations.description: Reorder loops so that the output spatial loops (OH, OW) iterate in the correct order relative to feature dimension F to maximize spatial reuse.
transformations.rationale: Correct loop order ensures that data accessed in nearby iterations remains in cache; poor ordering causes thrashing.

transformations.name: Promote Reduction Loop Position
transformations.description: Move the reduction loop (over input channel C or filter spatial KH×KW) to an optimal position (typically innermost after outer blocking loops) to maximize vectorization and minimize memory traffic.
transformations.rationale: Innermost reduction loops are most amenable to vectorization and pipelined execution; outer reductions cause suboptimal register usage and poor parallelism.

intents.name: Data Packing & Bufferization
intents.description: Pre-process and repack tensor data into cache-oblivious or cache-aware layouts to improve access patterns and reduce memory fragmentation.
intents.rationale: Raw tensor layouts may not match access patterns of the optimized kernel. Packing (e.g., grouping filter channels into blocks, transposing) can eliminate strided access and improve cache utilization.

transformations.name: Pack Filters into Block Layout
transformations.description: Repack filter tensor (F×C×KH×KW) into a blocked layout that groups C channels and output features F into cache-friendly blocks.
transformations.rationale: Grouped layout reduces the number of cache misses when iterating over filters; enables contiguous load patterns.

transformations.name: Pack Input Activations into Tiles
transformations.description: Pre-tile input spatial patches (H×W per channel) into smaller rectangular buffers that fit in L2 cache.
transformations.rationale: Reduces working set per tile and can eliminate capacity misses; enables sequential, high-throughput data access within each tile.

transformations.name: Allocate Temporary Buffers for Intermediate Results
transformations.description: Introduce explicitly-managed small buffers (stack or L1-sized) for intermediate partial sums or tile results.
transformations.rationale: Keeps intermediate values in fast memory (L1 or registers) rather than spilling to main memory; critical for kernels with high arithmetic intensity.

intents.name: Coarse-Grain Parallelization
intents.description: Distribute outer loop iterations (N, F, OH, OW tiles) across CPU cores to exploit multi-socket and NUMA topology.
intents.rationale: The target CPU has 28 cores across 2 NUMA sockets. Parallelizing outer tiled loops (one tile per core) enables linear scaling up to ~14 cores per socket. Must respect NUMA locality to avoid inter-socket traffic.

transformations.name: Parallelize Output Tile Loops
transformations.description: Distribute outer loops over output spatial tiles (e.g., tiled OH, OW) across threads with affinity to NUMA nodes.
transformations.rationale: Tiles are independent; each thread can compute its tile without synchronization. Affinity ensures each thread accesses its input/filter data locally.

transformations.name: Parallelize Feature Tile Loops
transformations.description: Parallelize the outer feature dimension loop (tiled F) across cores to balance output channel computation.
transformations.rationale: Feature-dimension parallelism is straightforward: each tile of output channels is independent. Reduces contention on shared caches.

transformations.name: NUMA-Aware Data Distribution
transformations.description: Bind data partitions (input tiles, filter blocks, output buffers) to NUMA nodes matching the thread affinity.
transformations.rationale: Reduces inter-socket traffic, which is ~10–20× slower than intra-socket memory access. Critical for large tensors on multi-socket systems.

intents.name: Loop Unrolling & Software Pipelining
intents.description: Unroll and software-pipeline innermost loops to increase instruction-level parallelism and hide memory latency.
intents.rationale: Modern CPUs have deep pipelines and multiple functional units. Unrolling and pipelining allow multiple independent operations to execute in parallel, hiding latencies and improving throughput.

transformations.name: Unroll Innermost Reduction Loop
transformations.description: Unroll the innermost loop (typically channel or filter dimension) by 2–8 iterations to expose independent FMA operations.
transformations.rationale: Reduces loop overhead and allows out-of-order execution of multiple independent FMAs; improves FU saturation and hides latencies.

transformations.name: Unroll Outer Spatial Loops
transformations.description: Selectively unroll outer spatial loops (OH, OW) by small factors to improve locality and register pressure trade-offs.
transformations.rationale: Moderate unrolling can improve register reuse and reduce spills; excessive unrolling causes register pressure and cache evictions.

transformations.name: Software Pipeline Inner Accumulation
transformations.description: Manually pipeline the accumulation loop so that independent FMA chains are interleaved to hide FMA latency (~5 cycles).
transformations.rationale: Hiding latency allows full FU utilization; critical on CPUs with deep pipelines and FMA latencies. Requires careful register allocation.

intents.name: Algorithmic & Numerical Specialization
intents.description: Apply precision reduction, special-case kernel variants, or problem-specific optimizations based on tensor properties.
intents.rationale: Convolution performance can be improved by exploiting problem structure: reduced precision (FP32 instead of FP64), specialized kernels for common filter sizes, or algorithmic variants (e.g., Winograd for small filters).

transformations.name: Precision Reduction (Conceptual)
transformations.description: Consider lowering from FP64 to FP32 to increase vector width (8 lanes vs. 4) and reduce memory bandwidth.
transformations.rationale: FP32 doubles vector lane count and halves memory footprint; may be acceptable for ML workloads with inherent numerical tolerance.

transformations.name: Winograd or FFT-Based Convolution (Specialized)
transformations.description: Decompose small filter convolutions (e.g., 3×3) into cheaper FFT or Winograd operations with reduced arithmetic cost.
transformations.rationale: Winograd reduces FLOPs for small filters (e.g., 3×3 filters by ~2–3×) but increases memory traffic and complexity; niche optimization for small filters.

transformations.name: Kernel Specialization by Filter Size
transformations.description: Instantiate specialized, hand-optimized kernels for common filter sizes (1×1, 3×3, 5×5) with pre-tuned parameters.
transformations.rationale: Specialized kernels can exploit structure (e.g., 1×1 convolution is a matrix multiply); reduces synthesis complexity and improves performance for common cases.

intents.name: Register & Memory Hierarchy Management
intents.description: Carefully manage register allocation, spills, and memory hierarchy usage to maximize compute efficiency and minimize stalls.
intents.rationale: Register pressure is a limiting factor in convolution kernels. Excessive unrolling or accumulation can cause register spills, degrading performance by 20–50%. Careful management of working sets is essential.

transformations.name: Register Reuse Optimization
transformations.description: Structure inner loops so that values (partial sums, input elements) are reused across multiple iterations without reloading.
transformations.rationale: Reusing values in registers rather than reloading from L1 cache reduces memory traffic and stalls.

transformations.name: Spill Avoidance via Loop Restructuring
transformations.description: Adjust tile sizes and loop unrolling to keep the working set within available registers (~16–32 FP values per CPU thread).
transformations.rationale: Spills to memory incur ~100–200 cycle penalties. Careful tile sizing prevents spills.

intents.name: Miscellaneous Compiler-Level Optimizations
intents.description: Apply standard compiler techniques such as dead-code elimination, constant propagation, and peeling to simplify the computation.
intents.rationale: These optimizations reduce overhead and improve clarity for downstream optimization. E.g., if strides or dilations are constant (1), loop bounds can be simplified.

transformations.name: Constant Propagation & Simplification
transformations.description: Propagate constant strides/dilations (dense<1>) to eliminate conditional logic and simplify loop bounds.
transformations.rationale: Reduces branch mispredictions and enables aggressive loop optimizations in backend.

transformations.name: Loop Bound Tightening
transformations.description: Tighten loop bounds by analyzing tensor dimensions and removing unnecessary iterations.
transformations.rationale: Reduces iteration count and enables better prefetching and pipelining.

transformations.name: Common Subexpression Elimination (CSE)
transformations.description: Identify and eliminate redundant address computations and indexing operations.
transformations.rationale: Reduces address generation overhead, particularly in spatial loop nests where indices are heavily computed.
